rationale: Record the scoped captured-metadata re-apply for the watched import and render families. `resetAfterCommit` re-applied Chromium-captured metadata across the WHOLE captured document on every qualifying commit -- O(document) work for an O(1) repaint -- which a Perfetto capture measured as bursts of 2139-9024 bridge calls costing 45-157ms and producing 86-190ms visible stalls, twice per pointer stroke plus once per 700ms status-banner throttle. The change is confined to Pulp-owned commit bookkeeping: the single global `materializedTreeDirty` boolean becomes an all-flag plus a set of dirty instance ids, `applyMaterializedImportMetadata` accepts that scope and skips bindings whose node is neither a scoped node nor a descendant of one, `__pulpRefreshMaterializedState__` moves inside the same gate, and `isEventHandler` is consulted by the paint-only and fixed-text-only gates so a recreated inline closure no longer dirties the tree. It does not change what the metadata MEANS, how a design is captured or ingested, or any transferred renderer, canvas, Skia, Graphite, Dawn, or resource implementation authority; a relationship change scopes to the parent because captured paths resolve through sibling indices, container-level mutations and root resizes still force the full pass, and an absent or empty scope applies everything so an older checked-in runtime artifact that ignores the new argument stays correct.
